title: Recall Quiz: Phonetics: Organs of Speech & Sounds

questions.q: Which organ is known as the soft palate?
questions.explanation: The velum is another name for the soft palate, responsible for nasal/oral sound distinction.

questions.q: What type of sound is produced when the vocal cords vibrate?
questions.explanation: Vibration of vocal cords produces voiced sounds.

questions.q: Which of the following is an active articulator?
questions.explanation: The tongue moves to create sounds, making it an active articulator.

questions.q: During the production of nasal sounds, the velum is:
questions.explanation: When the velum is lowered, air escapes through the nose, creating nasal sounds.

questions.q: The opening between the vocal cords is called the:
questions.explanation: The glottis is the space between the vocal cords.

questions.q: Which organ is a small, fleshy flap hanging at the back of the soft palate?
questions.explanation: The uvula hangs from the end of the velum.

questions.q: Which of these is a bilabial sound?
Where is the alveolar ridge located?
options: At the back of the throat
On the roof of the mouth
questions.explanation: The alveolar ridge is the bumpy area just behind the upper front teeth.

questions.q: A sound made by completely blocking the airflow and then releasing it suddenly is a:
questions.explanation: Plosives involve a complete stoppage of air followed by a sudden release.

questions.q: How many consonant sounds are there in Standard English?
questions.explanation: There are 24 consonant phonemes in English.
